summary: Cosmic Lens is an open-source, interactive web platform and scientific pipeline developed to explore multi-epoch NASA SPHEREx spectrophotometric survey data (0.75–5.00 µm). It addresses the challenge of mining petabyte-scale sky surveys by ingesting SPHEREx FITS cutouts, subtracting zodiacal dust, performing matched image differencing, and automating cross-matches against ESA Gaia DR3, NASA AllWISE, 2MASS, and the JPL Small-Body Identification API. Users can blink multi-epoch images, detect moving asteroids, and extract 102-channel spectra to analyze ices and atmospheres. Cosmic Lens bridges professional astronomy and citizen science, empowering the global public to rapidly discover Near-Earth Objects, brown dwarfs, and stellar transients with full scientific rigor.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Cosmic Lens is an open-source web platform and automated scientific pipeline designed to analyze NASA's SPHEREx all-sky spectrophotometric survey (0.75–5.00 µm). The platform ingests calibrated Level 2 multi-extension FITS images, models and subtracts zodiacal dust foregrounds, and performs flux-conserving spatial reprojection between observation epochs. It applies matched temporal image differencing and circular aperture photometry to isolate moving objects and brightness variations. Detected candidates across epochs are linked into motion vectors, and full 102-band calibrated spectra are extracted in real time.

BENEFITS AND ADVANTAGES

Cosmic Lens eliminates the barrier of complex software installation and manual FITS handling for researchers and citizen scientists. It automates false-positive filtering by cross-matching detections in real time against ESA Gaia DR3, NASA AllWISE, and 2MASS catalogs to flag stationary stars. Furthermore, it polls NASA/JPL’s Small-Body Identification API to instantly distinguish known asteroids from uncataloged discoveries. Users get an intuitive multi-band blink comparator, instant spectral analysis, and downloadable scientific audit receipts.

INTENDED IMPACT

With SPHEREx surveying the entire sky multiple times, the volume of data will produce hundreds of thousands of candidate transients that automated pipelines alone cannot thoroughly vet. Cosmic Lens democratizes astronomical discovery, enabling global volunteers and researchers to rapidly uncover Near-Earth Objects (NEOs), planetary defense targets, cold brown dwarfs, and rare stellar outbursts. Every vetted candidate can be exported with full provenance to tools like WiseView and the Minor Planet Center.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, AND SOFTWARE USED

- Languages: Python 3.11 (backend processing) and TypeScript (frontend user interface).

- Scientific Stack: Astropy, Photutils, Reproject, and Astroquery for WCS math, aperture photometry, image warping, and archive queries.

- Web Frameworks: FastAPI and Uvicorn for asynchronous REST APIs; Next.js 14 and Tailwind CSS for a fast, responsive interface.

- APIs and Data Archives: NASA/IPAC IRSA (SPHEREx, WISE, 2MASS), NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics (SSD) API, ESA Gaia DR3 via CDS VizieR, and CADC for CSA NEOSSat data.

- Visualization: Custom interactive SVG sky canvas and CDS Aladin Lite v3 for multi-wavelength all-sky context.

CREATIVITY AND INNOVATION

Traditional transient discovery platforms rely purely on black-and-white optical blinking. Cosmic Lens innovates by bringing 102-channel infrared spectrophotometry directly into the browser. Users do not just see a dot moving; they can click any candidate to extract an on-the-fly spectrum, instantly identifying diagnostic chemical absorption bands like water ice (3.0 µm) and carbon dioxide ice (4.26 µm). It also introduces a "Receipt Drawer" providing cryptographic provenance and processing parameters for every candidate, ensuring scientific reproducibility.

KEY FACTORS AND DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS

- Scientific Rigor: Strict adherence to real NASA data—no synthetic or hardcoded candidate data in production.

- Astrometric Precision: Sub-pixel centroid alignment and handling SPHEREx's Low Earth Orbit parallax baseline.

- Zero-Barrier Accessibility: Offloading heavy array computations to an asynchronous backend so the platform runs smoothly on any device without requiring users to install scientific Python libraries.
